title: Human Health and Disease
syllabus: Health and Disease; Pathogens; Parasites causing human diseases (Malaria, Filariasis, Ascariasis, Typhoid, Pneumonia, Common cold, Amoebiasis, Ringworm, Dengue, Chikungunya); Basic concepts of immunology - vaccines; Cancer, HIV and AIDS; Adolescence, drug and alcohol abuse; Tobacco abuse.

questions.question: Which of the following diagnostic laboratory tests is used for the definitive confirmation of Typhoid fever?
questions.solution: Typhoid fever, caused by the pathogenic bacterium Salmonella typhi, is confirmed in the laboratory using the serological Widal test based on antigen-antibody agglutination.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding infectious diseases and their causative pathogenic agents:

List-I (Infectious Disease)List-II (Causative Pathogen)
(A) Pneumonia(I) Rhino viruses
(B) Common cold(II) Streptococcus pneumoniae & Haemophilus influenzae
(C) Amoebiasis(III) Entamoeba histolytica
(D) Ringworm(IV) Microsporum, Trichophyton & Epidermophyton

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Pneumonia is caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae; Common cold by Rhino viruses; Amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery) by Entamoeba histolytica; Ringworm by fungi belonging to genera Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton.

questions.question: Pneumonia infects the alveoli of the lungs, causing them to get filled with fluid leading to severe breathing difficulties. In severe cases of pneumonia, which characteristic diagnostic sign appears?
options: Lips and fingernails turn gray to bluish in color
Chronic swelling of the lower limbs and scrotum
Nasal congestion and discharge without alveolar involvement
questions.solution: In severe cases of pneumonia, due to inadequate oxygenation of arterial blood, the lips and fingernails may turn gray to bluish (cyanosis). In contrast, the common cold infects the nose and respiratory passage, but not the lungs.

questions.question: The infectious, motile form of Plasmodium that is injected into the human bloodstream through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito is called:
questions.solution: The infectious stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body via the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito is the sporozoite.

questions.question: The recurring recurring chills and high fever recurring every 3 to 4 days in a malaria patient are caused by the periodic release of which toxic substance upon rupture of infected erythrocytes (RBCs)?
questions.solution: Rupture of erythrocytic schizonts releases merozoites along with a toxic byproduct of hemoglobin breakdown called haemozoin, which is responsible for the recurring chills and high fever every 3 to 4 days.

questions.question: Sexual reproduction (fertilization and development of gametocytes into sporozoites) of the malaria parasite Plasmodium takes place in the:
options: Gut and salivary glands of the female Anopheles mosquito
Liver cells (hepatocytes) of the human host
Red blood cells of the human host
Blood plasma of the human host
questions.solution: Gametocytes (sexual stages) develop in human RBCs, but fertilization and zygote development into sporozoites take place in the stomach wall and gut of the female Anopheles mosquito, after which mature sporozoites migrate to its salivary glands.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding vector-borne and helminthic diseases:

List-I (Disease)List-II (Causative Organism / Vector)
(A) Filariasis (Elephantiasis)(I) Ascaris lumbricoides (intestinal roundworm)
(B) Ascariasis(II) Wuchereria bancrofti & W. malayi (transmitted by female Culex)
(C) Dengue & Chikungunya(III) Female Aedes mosquito
(D) Amoebic dysentery(IV) Houseflies (Musca domestica) acting as mechanical carriers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Filariasis: Filarial worms Wuchereria transmitted by female Culex mosquito; Ascariasis: Ascaris; Dengue/Chikungunya: Transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; Amoebiasis: Entamoeba mechanically transmitted by houseflies via contaminated water/food.

questions.question: Chronic inflammation and deformities of the lymphatic vessels of lower limbs and genital organs (Elephantiasis) are characteristic symptoms of:
questions.solution: Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi), the filarial worms, cause a slowly developing chronic inflammation of the organs in which they live for many years, usually the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs (elephantiasis or filariasis) and genital deformities.

questions.question: Internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anemia, and intestinal blockage are typical clinical symptoms of infection by which intestinal endoparasite?
questions.solution: Ascaris, an intestinal parasite, causes ascariasis. Symptoms include internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anemia, and blockage of the intestinal passage. Eggs of the parasite are excreted in feces and contaminate soil, water, and plants.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Innate Immunity barriers in humans:

List-I (Innate Barrier Category)List-II (Examples / Physiological Component)
(A) Physical barriers(I) Lysozyme in tears/saliva and $\text{HCl}$ in stomach
(B) Physiological barriers(II) Skin (stratum corneum) and mucus coating of respiratory/urogenital tracts
(C) Cellular barriers(III) Polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNL), Monocytes, and Natural Killer (NK) cells
(D) Cytokine barriers(IV) Interferons secreted by virus-infected cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Physical: Skin and mucosal epithelium; Physiological: Stomach $\text{HCl}$, saliva, tears; Cellular: PMNL-neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, NK cells; Cytokine: Interferons (proteins produced by virus-infected cells to protect non-infected cells).

questions.question: Proteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect non-infected neighbouring cells from further viral replication are called:
questions.solution: Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons (cytokine barrier of innate immunity) which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.

questions.question: An antibody molecule is represented as $\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$ because each functional antibody monomer is composed of:
options: Two identical heavy polypeptide chains and two identical light polypeptide chains joined by disulfide bonds
Two heavy chains and one light chain
Two lipid chains and two polysaccharide chains
questions.solution: Each antibody molecule has four peptide chains: two small light (L) chains and two longer heavy (H) chains connected by interchain disulfide bridges, hence represented as $\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$.

questions.question: Which branch of acquired immunity is primarily mediated by T-lymphocytes and is responsible for graft rejection during organ transplantation?
questions.solution: Cell-Mediated Immunity (CMI), mediated by T-lymphocytes (specifically cytotoxic T-cells), is responsible for the body's ability to differentiate 'self' from 'non-self' and triggers the rejection of allografts/grafts in organ transplantation.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Immunity:

List-I (Type of Immunity)List-II (Defining Feature / Example)
(A) Active Natural Immunity(I) Injection of pre-formed antitoxin/antivenom antibodies after a snakebite
(B) Active Artificial Immunity(II) Developing lifelong immunity following natural recovery from chickenpox/measles
(C) Passive Natural Immunity(III) Vaccination with attenuated microbes (e.g., Polio vaccine, MMR)
(D) Passive Artificial Immunity(IV) Transfer of maternal secretory IgA via colostrum and IgG across placenta

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Active natural: Natural infection and recovery; Active artificial: Vaccines; Passive natural: Maternal IgA (colostrum) and IgG (transplacental); Passive artificial: Administration of pre-formed antibodies (anti-tetanus serum, anti-snake venom).

questions.question: Recombinant DNA technology has enabled the large-scale production of Hepatitis-B vaccine using which transgenic eukaryotic host organism?
questions.solution: Hepatitis-B vaccine is a second-generation subunit recombinant vaccine produced from transgenic brewer's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

questions.question: Allergy is an exaggerated immune response to foreign environmental antigens (allergens). It is primarily mediated by antibodies of which immunoglobulin class?
questions.solution: Allergies are mediated by IgE antibodies. Exposure to allergens triggers mast cells to degranulate and release inflammatory chemicals like histamine and serotonin.

questions.question: Which of the following is an autoimmune disorder in which the immune system fails to recognize self-antigens and attacks synovial joints?
questions.solution: Rheumatoid arthritis is a classic autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system attacks its own tissues, specifically the synovial membranes of joints, causing chronic inflammation and deformity.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Primary and Secondary Lymphoid Organs:

List-I (Lymphoid Organ Category)List-II (Anatomical Examples & Functional Role)
(A) Primary Lymphoid Organs(I) Spleen, Lymph nodes, Tonsils, Peyer's patches, and Appendix
(B) Secondary Lymphoid Organs(II) Bone marrow and Thymus (where immature lymphocytes differentiate)
(C) MALT (Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue)(III) Constitutes about 50 per cent of the total lymphoid tissue in human body

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Primary lymphoid organs (Bone marrow and Thymus) are sites of lymphocyte maturation; Secondary lymphoid organs (Spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches) provide sites for interaction with antigens; MALT constitutes ~50% of human lymphoid tissue.

questions.question: Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) is located within the mucosal lining of major tracts (respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts) and constitutes approximately what percentage of the total lymphoid tissue in the human body?
questions.solution: MALT (Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue) constitutes about 50 per cent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.

questions.question: The genetic material of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) consists of:
options: Two identical molecules of single-stranded RNA (+ssRNA) and reverse transcriptase
questions.solution: HIV is an enveloped retrovirus possessing a protein capsid enclosing two identical copies of single-stranded RNA (+ssRNA) along with the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

questions.question: Once HIV enters the human body, which immune cells act as an 'HIV factory' continuously producing new viral particles?
questions.solution: After entering the body, HIV enters macrophages where viral RNA replicates into viral DNA via reverse transcriptase. Macrophages continuously produce virus particles and act like an 'HIV factory'.

questions.question: The progressive destruction of which specific immune cell population leads to the profound immunodeficiency seen in AIDS patients, making them susceptible to opportunistic infections like Mycobacterium, toxoplasma, and fungi?
questions.solution: HIV infects and replicates inside $\text{T}_H$ cells (helper T-lymphocytes/CD4+), leading to a progressive decrease in the number of helper T-cells in the infected person, resulting in severe immunodeficiency against opportunistic pathogens.

questions.question: Which of the following screening tests is widely used as a primary diagnostic tool for the detection of HIV infection?
questions.solution: A widely used diagnostic test for AIDS/HIV screening is ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay), followed by confirmatory Western Blot testing.

questions.question: Normal cells show a regulatory property where contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth and division. Cancer cells lose this property, which is called:
questions.solution: Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled proliferation. Cancer cells appear to have lost this property, dividing continuously to form tumors.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most dreaded and distinctive property of malignant neoplastic tumors?
options: Metastasis (sloughing off and invading distant sites via blood/lymph)
questions.solution: Metastasis is the most feared property of malignant tumors: cancerous cells slough off from the primary tumor, reach distant organs through the bloodstream, lodge in new tissues, and start growing new secondary tumors.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding types of Carcinogens (cancer-causing agents):

List-I (Carcinogen Category)List-II (Specific Agent / Example)
(A) Physical carcinogens (Ionizing radiation)(I) Tobacco smoke (major cause of lung cancer)
(B) Physical carcinogens (Non-ionizing radiation)(II) X-rays and gamma rays
(C) Chemical carcinogens(III) UV-rays (causes DNA thymine dimers)
(D) Biological carcinogens(IV) Oncogenic viruses (possessing viral oncogenes)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Ionizing radiation: X-rays, gamma rays; Non-ionizing radiation: UV rays; Chemical carcinogens: Chemical mutagens in tobacco smoke; Biological carcinogens: Oncogenic viruses carrying v-onc genes.

questions.question: Genes present in normal human cells which, when activated under certain conditions, can lead to oncogenic transformation of the cells are called:
questions.solution: Several genes called cellular oncogenes (c-onc) or proto-oncogenes have been identified in normal cells which, when activated under specific mutational conditions, cause oncogenic transformation into cancerous cells.

questions.question: In cancer immunotherapy, biological response modifiers administered to patients to activate their immune system and help destroy tumors are:
questions.solution: Tumor cells often evade detection and destruction by the immune system. Patients are given substances called biological response modifiers such as $\alpha$-interferon which activate their immune system and help destroy tumors.

questions.question: Opioid drugs (such as morphine and heroin) bind to specific opioid receptors located in the:
options: Central Nervous System (CNS) and Gastrointestinal tract
questions.solution: Opioids are drugs that bind to specific opioid receptors present in our central nervous system (CNS) and gastrointestinal tract.

questions.question: Heroin, commonly called 'smack', is chemically diacetylmorphine. It is synthesized by the acetylation of morphine extracted from the latex of:
questions.solution: Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is a white, odorless, bitter crystalline compound obtained by the acetylation of morphine, which is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant Papaver somniferum. It is a depressant that slows down body functions.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding classes of abused drugs, their source plants, and physiological effects:

List-I (Drug Category)List-II (Source Plant & Physiological Action)
(A) Opioids (Heroin)(I) Cannabis sativa; affects the cardiovascular system of the body
(B) Cannabinoids (Marijuana, Charas, Ganja)(II) Papaver somniferum; depressant that slows down body functions
(C) Coca alkaloid (Cocaine / 'Coke')(I) Erythroxylum coca; interferes with dopamine transport and stimulates CNS
(D) Hallucinogens(IV) Atropa belladonna & Datura; produce profound hallucinations

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Opioids (from Papaver somniferum): CNS depressants; Cannabinoids (from Cannabis sativa): Affect cardiovascular system; Cocaine (from Erythroxylum coca): Blocks dopamine reuptake causing euphoria and energy; Atropa and Datura have hallucinogenic properties.

questions.question: Cannabinoid receptors are principally located in the human body inside the:
questions.solution: Natural cannabinoids interact with cannabinoid receptors present principally in the brain. They are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system of the body.

questions.question: Cocaine (coca alkaloid / 'coke' / 'crack') is extracted from the leaves of Erythroxylum coca native to South America. It produces a potent stimulating action on the CNS by interfering with the transport of which neurotransmitter?
questions.solution: Cocaine interferes with the reuptake and transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine, producing a potent stimulation of the CNS, inducing a sense of euphoria and increased energy. Excessive dosage causes hallucinations.

questions.question: Which of the following plants possess strong hallucinogenic properties and are often abused?
questions.solution: Plants with well-known hallucinogenic properties include Atropa belladonna and species of Datura (as well as LSD derived from the ergot fungus Claviceps purpurea).

questions.question: Tobacco smoke contains nicotine, an alkaloid that stimulates the adrenal glands to release which hormones into blood circulation, leading to raised blood pressure and increased heart rate?
questions.solution: Tobacco contains nicotine, which stimulates the adrenal gland to release adrenaline and noradrenaline into blood circulation, both of which raise blood pressure and increase heart rate.

questions.question: Smoking is associated with increased incidence of cancers of lung, urinary bladder, and throat, bronchitis, emphysema, and coronary heart disease. Smoking increases the level of which gas in blood, leading to oxygen deficiency?
options: Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$), reducing the concentration of haembound oxygen
questions.solution: Smoking increases carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) content in blood and reduces the concentration of haembound oxygen, causing hypoxia in body tissues.

questions.question: Dependence on drugs or alcohol is defined as the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant syndrome if regular doses are abruptly discontinued. This syndrome is known as:
options: Withdrawal syndrome (anxiety, shakiness, nausea, and sweating)
questions.solution: Dependence is the tendency of the body to manifest a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome if regular dose of drugs/alcohol is abruptly discontinued. It is characterized by anxiety, shakiness, nausea, and sweating, which may be relieved when use is resumed.

questions.question: Chronic heavy intake of alcohol over prolonged periods leads to severe liver damage characterized by replacement of healthy liver tissue with non-functional fibrous scar tissue, known as:
questions.solution: Chronic heavy use of alcohol damages the nervous system and liver, leading to liver cirrhosis (fibrosis of hepatic parenchyma).

questions.question: Side-effects of the use of anabolic steroids in adolescent females include:
options: Masculinisation, increased aggressiveness, mood swings, abnormal menstrual cycles, excessive body hair, and enlargement of clitoris
Excessive milk production and breast enlargement
Reduction in bone density and dwarfism exclusively
Severe drop in blood glucose with coma
questions.solution: The side-effects of anabolic steroids in females include masculinisation, increased aggressiveness, mood swings, depression, abnormal menstrual cycles, excessive facial and body hair growth, deepening of voice, and enlargement of the clitoris.

questions.question: Which of the following approaches is most critical for the prevention and control of drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents?
options: Avoiding undue peer pressure, education and counselling, seeking help from parents/peers, and seeking professional/medical help
Isolating the adolescent in solitary confinement
Administering high doses of sedative tranquilizers
Encouraging competitive comparison with high achievers
questions.solution: Preventive measures outlined by NCERT include: (1) Avoid undue peer pressure, (2) Education and counselling, (3) Seeking help from parents and peers, (4) Looking for danger signs, and (5) Seeking professional psychological and medical de-addiction help.

questions.question: Ringworm infection is characterized by dry, scaly lesions on various parts of the body such as skin, nails, and scalp, accompanied by intense itching. The fungi thrive particularly well in:
options: Heat and moisture in skin folds (such as groin or between toes)
questions.solution: Heat and moisture help ringworm fungi (Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton) to grow in skin folds, such as in the groin or between the toes (Athlete's foot).

questions.question: Fish like Gambusia are introduced into ponds and water reservoirs because they:
options: Feed on mosquito larvae, helping biological control of malaria and dengue vectors
Eliminate water weeds that harbor fungi
questions.solution: Larvivorous fishes like Gambusia are introduced into water bodies to feed on mosquito larvae, acting as an effective biological control method against vector-borne diseases like malaria, filariasis, and dengue.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Primary immune response to a pathogen is of low intensity and slow, while secondary (anamnestic) response is rapid and highly intensified due to immunological memory.
Statement II: B-lymphocytes produce an army of proteins called antibodies in response to pathogens, while T-cells help B-cells produce them.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The primary response is slow and low-intensity; subsequent exposure to the same pathogen elicits a heightened anamnestic response based on memory cells. B-cells produce circulating antibodies, and T-helper cells facilitate this humoral response.

questions.question: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a safe and highly accurate diagnostic technique for detecting cancer in internal organs because it uses:
options: Strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiations to accurately detect pathological and physiological changes in living tissues
Ultrasound shockwaves that disrupt tumor membranes
questions.solution: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiations to accurately detect pathological and physiological changes in living tissue, avoiding radiation damage.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding NACO and AIDS prevention:
Statement I: National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) educate people about AIDS prevention in India.
Statement II: Transmission of HIV infection from mother to child can never be reduced by any medical treatment.

Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because prophylactic antiretroviral therapy (ART) given to HIV-infected pregnant mothers significantly reduces the rate of vertical transmission to the newborn.
